# Messaging

`pb.messaging` is the signed-in person's conversations in the browser: their list, each conversation's timeline and its threads, kept in IndexedDB between visits and current over the project's socket. An app subscribes to what it draws and writes; it opens no socket, appends nothing and syncs nothing itself. What the module is — history, encryption, files, timers, moderation, prices — is [Messaging](/docs/messaging/overview).

## Quick example

```ts
// src/lib/palbase.ts
import { createClient } from "palbase/web";

export const pb = createClient({
  url: "https://k3xq81w4m.palbase.studio",
  publishableKey: "pb_k3xq81w4m_cZ8yX7wV6uT5",
  // What the browser keeps of the person's conversations when they sign out: dropped unless true.
  messaging: { keepOnSignOut: false },
});
```

```ts
// src/inbox.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

// The person's conversations, the latest first: drawn from the device at once, then kept current.
const list = pb.messaging.conversations();
const stopList = list.subscribe(() => {
  const { items, unread, synced } = list.state;
  console.log(`${unread} unread in ${items.length} conversations`, synced ? "" : "(catching up)");
});

// The direct conversation with someone: the one there is, or a new one (it shows to them with its first message).
const chat = await pb.messaging.direct("usr_01a1684c796e7394aa8ec75d893a8fe2");
const stopChat = chat.subscribe(() => {
  for (const entry of chat.state.entries) {
    if (entry.kind === "message") console.log(entry.message.sender_id, entry.message.text);
    else console.log("sending…", entry.item.request.text, entry.item.state);
  }
});

// Drawn at once, sent now or when the network is back — once.
await chat.send("Hi!");
await chat.markRead();

stopChat();
stopList();
```

## Conversations

| Call | What it is |
|---|---|
| `conversations({ spaces })` | The person's conversations, the latest first: `items`, `unread` across them, and `synced` once the device's copy caught up — of some spaces alone when it names any ([Spaces and open groups](#spaces-and-open-groups)) |
| `conversation(id)` | One conversation: `conversation`, `entries` (its timeline, the oldest first, then what is on its way), `members`, `typing`, `hasEarlier`; opened at a message (`{ at }`), `focus` and `hasLater` too ([Search](#search)) |
| `direct(userId, { space })` | The direct conversation with someone — in a space, when it names one |
| `group({ title, memberIds, description, photo, settings, space, visibility })` | A new group, the person its owner; `notAdded` names whom the project's hook kept out |
| `openGroups(space, { limit, cursor })` | A space's open groups, each with whether the person is in it (`joined`) |
| `join(conversationId)` | Joins an open group: the conversation, the person in it |
| `thread(conversationId, rootId)` | A message's thread: `root`, `entries`, `thread` (its count, its last answer, who answered, its unread count) |
| `threads()` | The threads the person follows |
| `scheduled()` | The person's messages for later |

Each view (`conversations()`, `conversation(id)`, `thread(…)`, `scheduled()`) is an `Observed`: `state` now and `subscribe(listener)`, which returns the call that stops it. It reads the device's copy while subscribed and as long as the person stays the same; when another person signs in, it reads theirs. `loadEarlier()` reads the page before the oldest message drawn.

```ts
// src/team.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

const team = await pb.messaging.group({ title: "Design", memberIds: ["usr_01a1684c796e7394aa8ec75d893a8fe2"] });
const view = team.conversation;
view.subscribe(() => console.log(view.state.members.length, "members,", view.state.typing.length, "typing"));
if (view.state.hasEarlier) await view.loadEarlier();
await pb.messaging.update(view.id, { title: "Design team" });
```

## Spaces and open groups

A person is often in several places of your app's — organizations, workspaces, projects. A conversation belongs to one when it is made with a `space` your app names (`org:<id>`, `project:<id>`; 1 to 128 letters, digits and `: _ . / @ -`), and stays there: the same two people have one direct conversation in each space, and one with none. `conversations({ spaces: [...] })` is a space's list, its `unread` that space's; `search(q, { space })` searches it. Each conversation says its `space` (`null`: none).

A group made with `visibility: 'open'` is found in its space's open groups and joined by the person themselves — a channel; a closed one (the default) is joined when someone adds you. Your server decides who may make one, find a space's groups and join them: the project's hook is asked (`open_group`, `list_open`, `join`, the space named) and its refusal is a `PalbaseError`, code `not_allowed`. An open group names its `space` (`space_required` otherwise). One an admin removed does not join again by themselves (`removed`); a full group is `group_full`.

```ts
// src/channels.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

const org = "org:2f6c0c1e-8a3b-4c1d-9e5f-0a1b2c3d4e5f";
const sidebar = pb.messaging.conversations({ spaces: [org] });
const general = await pb.messaging.group({ title: "general", space: org, visibility: "open" });
const channels = await pb.messaging.openGroups(org);
for (const c of channels.items) if (!c.joined) await pb.messaging.join(c.id);
const dm = await pb.messaging.direct("usr_01a1684c796e7394aa8ec75d893a8fe2", { space: org });
```

A message your server wrote as someone (an assistant sending their words) says so: `message.via` names what wrote it (`"pal"`) — draw it beside the message, as "sent by Pal".

## Writing

`send(conversationId, input)` — or a view's own `send(input)` — takes text or what a message carries:

```ts
// src/compose.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

const conversationId = "0199f0c2-6a3e-7b1d-9f4e-2d1c8b7a6e50";
const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=file]")!;
const photo = input.files![0];

// Answers a message inline, mentions someone, carries a file encrypted on this device before it is uploaded.
await pb.messaging.send(conversationId, {
  text: "Here it is, @bob",
  replyTo: "0199f0c2-7c11-7e2f-8a3b-4c5d6e7f8091",
  files: [{ data: photo, contentType: photo.type, name: photo.name }],
});

// In a thread, shown in the conversation too; gone a day after everyone read it.
await pb.messaging.send(conversationId, { text: "Agreed", threadId: "0199f0c2-7c11-7e2f-8a3b-4c5d6e7f8091", alsoInConversation: true, expiresIn: 86_400, expiresFrom: "read" });

// Seen once: its photo opens for ten seconds, once.
await pb.messaging.send(conversationId, { files: [{ data: photo, contentType: photo.type }], viewOnce: { limit: 1, seconds: 10 } });

// Sent tomorrow at nine by the server, the browser closed or not: scheduled() lists it until then.
const nine = new Date();
nine.setDate(nine.getDate() + 1);
nine.setHours(9, 0, 0, 0);
await pb.messaging.send(conversationId, { text: "Good morning", sendAt: nine });
```

A message waits in the outbox while the browser is offline or the server is away and goes once it can, once; an entry of kind `pending` is one on its way. `edit`, `remove` (for `everyone` or `me`), `react` and `unreact`, `markRead`, `typing`, `cancelScheduled` and `editScheduled` change what was said. `open(message, attachmentId)` downloads a file and decrypts it in the browser; a message seen once gives its files by `viewOnce(message)` alone, and the app holds them — the device keeps none.

## Search

`search(query, { conversationId, space, limit, cursor })` finds the person's messages that say every word asked — a word's beginning finds it, "toplanti" finds "Toplantıda" — the newest first, across their conversations or in one. Each hit carries what a result row draws: the conversation's `title` and `photo` (a group's, or the other person's in a direct one), its `sender`, `peer`, and its `matches` — where its text or a file's name says what was asked, in UTF-16 code units, as a string's. The first page also lists the person's conversations whose name says it (`conversations`), from their own list. What the module finds and never finds: [Messaging](/docs/messaging/overview#search).

A find opens where it was said: `conversation(id, { at })` is the conversation's stretch around the message, `focus` naming it to scroll to and mark. `loadEarlier()` reads back from there and `loadLater()` forward; once it reaches the newest, `hasLater` is false and it is the conversation's timeline again. An answer the conversation's timeline does not show has a `threadRootId`: open its thread at it.

```ts
// src/search.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

const found = await pb.messaging.search("toplanti");
for (const c of found.conversations) console.log(c.title); // their names say it: draw them first

const mark = (text: string, at: { offset: number; length: number }[]) =>
  at.reduceRight((t, m) => `${t.slice(0, m.offset)}<b>${t.slice(m.offset, m.offset + m.length)}</b>${t.slice(m.offset + m.length)}`, text);
for (const hit of found.messages) {
  console.log(hit.title, mark(hit.message.text ?? "", hit.matches.filter((m) => m.field === "text")));
}

// Tapped: opened at the message, the message marked.
const hit = found.messages[0];
const at = hit.threadRootId
  ? pb.messaging.thread(hit.conversation.id, hit.threadRootId, { at: hit.message.id })
  : pb.messaging.conversation(hit.conversation.id, { at: hit.message.id });
at.subscribe(() => console.log(at.state.entries.length, "around", at.state.focus));

// More: while nextCursor is not null.
const more = found.nextCursor ? await pb.messaging.search("toplanti", { cursor: found.nextCursor }) : null;
```

### By meaning

With the project's `search_by_meaning` on ([Messaging](/docs/messaging/overview#by-meaning)), `search(query, { by: "meaning" })` finds the messages nearest what the question means, in none of its words: "uçuş saati kaçta" finds "Uçağımız sabah dokuzda Sabiha Gökçen'den kalkıyor". The nearest come first, one page (`nextCursor` is null), each with `score` — how near, 0.3 to 1 — and no `matches`; `conversations` is empty. A hit opens as any does: `conversation(id, { at })`.

```ts
// src/search-meaning.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

try {
  const found = await pb.messaging.search("uçuş saati kaçta", { by: "meaning" });
  for (const hit of found.messages) console.log(hit.score?.toFixed(2), hit.title, hit.message.text);
} catch (e) {
  // search_by_meaning_off (409): the project searches by words alone — offer that.
  // too_many_searches (429): a person asks 30 at once, one more a minute; e.retryAfter says when.
  // ai_payment_required (402): the project's AI use is spent for the month.
  console.log((e as { code?: string }).code);
}
```

## A message while the app is open

A push for a message is not shown as the browser's notification while a page of the app is in front: the service worker leaves it to the page. `onIncoming` tells the page a new message from someone else as it arrives, so it draws its own banner — skip the conversation already on the screen:

```ts
// src/banner.ts
import type { Message } from "palbase/web";
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

let open: string | null = null; // the conversation on the screen

const stop = pb.messaging.onIncoming((message: Message) => {
  if (message.conversation_id === open) return;
  console.log("banner:", message.sender_id, message.text ?? "sent a file");
});
stop();
```

## The person

`me()` and `updateMe({ name, image, read_receipts, show_last_seen, default_timer_seconds })` are the person's own profile and settings; `profiles(userIds)` others' names and pictures. `block(userId)`, `unblock(userId)` and `report({ … })` are theirs to use. `notifications(conversationId, { notify_level, muted_until })` mutes a conversation, or keeps only its mentions.

## A deleted group

When a group's owner or an admin deletes it — or its last member leaves — it goes from everyone's `conversations()` at once, and those who were in it can still report it for 14 days ([Messaging](/docs/messaging/overview#moderation)). `deletedGroups()` lists them while they can, the latest to stop first: `state.items` are `{ id, title, deletedBy, reportableUntil }`, and one goes at its `reportableUntil`. `report` names it by its id with no message; the last 30 messages the person saw in it go with the report. A group the project's server deleted is not among them.

```ts
// src/deleted.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

const deleted = pb.messaging.deletedGroups();
const stop = deleted.subscribe(() => {
  for (const g of deleted.state.items) console.log(g.title ?? "a group", "reportable until", g.reportableUntil);
});

const [group] = deleted.state.items;
if (group) await pb.messaging.report({ conversation_id: group.id, reason: "harassment", user_id: group.deletedBy ?? undefined });
stop();
```

The title is the one the device had; it is null when the device no longer had the group as the word came — on the deleter's own device now and then.

## Vanish mode and screenshots

A direct conversation in vanish mode (`update(id, { settings: { vanish: true } })`) drops what the person read when they leave it: call `close(conversationId)` as its screen goes. A browser cannot know of a screenshot; the phone apps tell the others ([Messaging](/docs/messaging/overview#screenshots)).

## Signing out

When the person signs out, what the browser kept of their conversations is dropped and nothing of theirs is followed — unless `keepOnSignOut` is true, when it is theirs again the next time they sign in here, and no one else who signs in reads it. `storage` replaces where it is kept (IndexedDB, unless given).



<!-- ===== web/calls ===== -->

# Calls

`pb.calls` is the signed-in person's voice and video calls in the browser: it rings the people called, hears the calls that ring this person, and runs a call's media — every call's, one to one or in a group, through the platform's media server. An app draws what a call's state says and calls what the person does; it opens no peer connection, sends no signal and keeps no heartbeat itself. `palbase/web/calls-ui` draws the screens for an app that wants them ready-made. What the module is — kinds of call, who may call whom, ringing, history, prices — is [Calls](/docs/calls/overview).

## Quick example

```ts
// src/lib/palbase.ts
import { createClient } from "palbase/web";

export const pb = createClient({
  url: "https://k3xq81w4m.palbase.studio",
  publishableKey: "pb_k3xq81w4m_cZ8yX7wV6uT5",
  // The others' voices play by themselves: true unless the app plays each stream itself.
  calls: { playAudio: true },
});
```

```ts
// src/call.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

// The microphone is asked for first; once it is allowed, every device of theirs rings.
const call = await pb.calls.voice("usr_01a1684c796e7394aa8ec75d893a8fe2");

const stop = call.subscribe(() => {
  const { phase, remote, endReason } = call.state;
  if (phase === "connected") console.log("talking with", remote.map((r) => r.name ?? r.userId).join(", "));
  if (phase === "ended") {
    console.log("ended:", endReason);
    stop();
  }
});

await call.setMicrophone(false); // muted
await call.leave(); // hung up — or, while it rings, canceled
```

```ts
// src/incoming.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

// The calls that ring this person while the page is open — and the one ringing as a tap on its notification opens it.
pb.calls.onIncoming((call) => {
  const { call: c, phase } = call.state;
  if (phase !== "incoming") return; // "invited": a huddle, joined with call.join()
  const caller = c.participants.find((p) => p.user_id === c.caller_id);
  if (confirm(`${caller?.name ?? c.caller_id} is calling. Answer?`)) void call.accept();
  else void call.decline();
});
```

## Making a call

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `voice(userIds, options)` | A voice call: one person (a direct call) or several (a group) |
| `video(userIds, options)` | A video call |
| `start(userIds, options)` | Either, `video` saying which |
| `join(callId, options)` | Comes into a group call this person was asked to — a huddle, one they declined or left — on this device |

Each answers the call's `CallSession` once it rings. This device's microphone (and camera) is asked for first, and a refusal rings no one ([Permissions and errors](#permissions-and-errors)). A call to someone who is calling this person that very moment is their call, answered.

| Option | What it is |
|---|---|
| `video` | A video call (`start` alone) |
| `ring` | Ring the people asked (the default); `false`: a group call they join when they like (a huddle) |
| `group` | A group call even with one person asked: others may be asked later |
| `conversationId` | The conversation it is made from: its members alone may be called, and it keeps the call as a message |
| `metadata` | The app's own words about the call, shown to those rung: 32 strings, 2 KiB at most |
| `callerName`, `callerImageUrl` | What those rung see of the caller; else their messaging profile's name and picture |
| `media` | A microphone (and camera) stream the app opened already: used as it is, and left open when the call ends |

## A call that rings

`pb.calls.onIncoming(listener)` hears each call that rings this person while the page is open, and the calls ringing as it opens — the person tapped the call's notification ([Ringing while the page is away](#ringing-while-the-page-is-away)). It answers the unsubscribe. A group call that rings no one comes too, in the phase `invited`.

| On the session | What it does |
|---|---|
| `accept(options)` | Answers on this device. The first of the person's devices (or tabs) to answer has the call; the others go to `elsewhere`. `accept({ video: false })` answers a video call by voice; `{ video: true }` a voice call with the camera on |
| `decline()` | Turns the call down on every device of the person's: a direct call ends; a group goes on, and may still be joined |
| `join(options)` | Comes into a group call this person was asked to: a huddle (`invited`). A session that is over joins nothing: `pb.calls.join(callId)` comes into the call again |

`accept` and `join` take `video` and `media` as making a call does.

`pb.calls.onCall(listener)` hears each call this page comes into — made, answered or joined here; `pb.calls.current` is the one it is in, or `null`. `pb.calls.ready()` follows the person's calls without making one (`start`, `join` and `onIncoming` do it themselves), and rejects when no one is signed in.

## What to draw

A session's `state` is what the app draws, and `subscribe(listener)` tells each change of it (it answers the unsubscribe):

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `phase` | `calling` (the person called is rung), `incoming` (this person is rung), `invited` (asked into a huddle), `connecting` (answered, the media on its way), `connected`, `reconnecting` (the network dropped for a moment), `elsewhere` (answered on another device or tab), `ended` |
| `endReason` | Why it ended for this device: the call's `end_reason` ([A call's life](/docs/calls/overview#a-calls-life)), or `left` (this person left a group that goes on), `declined`, `missed`, `answered_elsewhere` |
| `call` | The call as the module last said it ([A call](/docs/calls/http#a-call)) |
| `me` | This person, as the call lists them |
| `outgoing` | This person rang, or started the group |
| `local` | This device's microphone and camera, while it is in the call: for its own preview |
| `microphone`, `camera` | Whether this device's microphone is heard and its camera on |
| `remote` | The others in the call (below) |
| `error` | The last thing that went wrong with this device's media: a camera refused, the media server not reached |

Each of `remote` is `userId` (an agent's is `bot:<identity>`), `name`, `imageUrl`, `bot`, `stream` — their audio and video, one `MediaStream` for the whole call, the same object whichever way the media flows — and whether they are heard (`audio`) and seen (`video`).

The others' voices play by themselves. With `calls: { playAudio: false }` in `createClient`'s options, each one's `stream` is the app's to play.

```ts
// src/call-view.ts
import type { CallSession } from "palbase/web";

/** Draws the others' video in a grid, and this device's camera in a corner. */
export function drawCall(session: CallSession, grid: HTMLElement, self: HTMLVideoElement): () => void {
  return session.subscribe(() => {
    const { remote, local } = session.state;
    self.srcObject = local;
    grid.replaceChildren(
      ...remote.map((r) => {
        const video = document.createElement("video");
        video.autoplay = true;
        video.playsInline = true;
        video.muted = true; // their voice already plays
        video.srcObject = r.stream;
        video.hidden = !r.video;
        return video;
      }),
    );
  });
}
```

## In the call

| On the session | What it does |
|---|---|
| `setMicrophone(on)` | The microphone heard, or muted |
| `setCamera(on)` | The camera on or off: off, it is closed and its light goes out; on, opened again — a voice call's too |
| `switchCamera(deviceId)` | Another camera: the one named (a `videoinput`'s `deviceId`), or, with none named, the other facing one |
| `setAudioOutput(deviceId)` | Where the others' voices play: an `audiooutput`'s `deviceId`, in a browser that can choose one |
| `invite(userIds, { ring })` | Asks more people in, ringing them unless `ring` is `false`: a direct call becomes a group, going on |
| `leave()` | Hangs up — or, while it rings, cancels: a direct call ends for both; a group goes on for the others |
| `refresh()` | Reads the call as it is now |

A page that goes away — closed, reloaded, navigated off — leaves its call at once.

## The media

Every call's media — one to one or in a group — goes through the platform's media server (LiveKit), through the LiveKit client the package depends on (`livekit-client`), loaded when the page's first call starts. The caller is in the call's room while it rings, so the media flows the moment it is answered; a third person or the project's agent comes into the same room, and the call goes on as it was. Where UDP is shut (a strict office or hotel network), the media goes over TCP to port 443 of the media server. When the network drops, the session is `reconnecting` while the client comes back into the room — with a new ticket if the room was lost — and what the app drew goes on playing.

What a call costs is the data the media server sent its people ([What it costs](/docs/calls/overview)): a voice call is a small part of a video call's.

## Ready-made screens

`palbase/web/calls-ui` draws the call screens in the page, with no framework: a sheet for a call that rings — who calls, by voice or with video, Decline and Accept, and for a video call Accept by voice too — and the view of the call this page is in: the others' video (their picture while their camera is off), this device's camera, how long it has gone on, and the microphone, the camera, the other camera and hang up.

```ts
// src/calls-ui.ts
import { mountCallUI } from "palbase/web/calls-ui";
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

const ui = mountCallUI(pb.calls, {
  theme: { accent: "#7c3aed", radius: 12 },
  texts: { incomingVoice: "Sesli arama", incomingVideo: "Görüntülü arama", accept: "Aç", decline: "Reddet" },
  ringtone: true,
  // A call from support is drawn by the app's own screen; the rest by these.
  incoming: (call) => call.metadata?.["kind"] !== "support",
  onError: (error) => console.warn("call:", error),
});

// Takes the screens away; a call going on goes on.
ui.unmount();
```

| Option | What it is |
|---|---|
| `container` | The element the screens are drawn in (positioned); the whole page unless given |
| `texts` | Every word the screens show, each replaced as given (`CALL_UI_TEXTS` has them all): the sheet's, the phases', and each way a call ends |
| `labels` | What a screen reader says of the buttons and views (`CALL_UI_LABELS`) |
| `theme` | `accent`, `background`, `foreground`, `danger`, `radius`, `font`, set as `--pb-call-<name>` on the screens' root; the system's light and dark colors unless given |
| `className` | Added to the root element's classes |
| `ringtone` | A soft ring while a sheet shows (the default); silent where the page may not play sound yet |
| `incoming(call, session)` | Asked once for each call that rings: `false` leaves it to the app's own screen, the session headless |
| `onError(error, session)` | An answer, a microphone or a camera that failed |

The newest ringing call is shown, the others wait behind it; a huddle rings no one and shows no sheet. The view goes two seconds after its call ends. What people say of themselves — a name, a picture — is set as text and as an image's address, never as markup.

## Ringing while the page is away

While no tab of the app is in front, a call rings this browser as a notification — the caller's name, and "Incoming voice call" or "Incoming video call" — shown by the SDK's service worker, `palbase-sw.js`, through the browser's push service. The browser must take the project's pushes: copy the worker into your site and subscribe it, as every web push needs ([Notifications](/docs/web/notifications#the-service-worker)). `pb.calls.deviceId` is the device the pushes are registered with.

- **A tab in front rings itself.** The worker shows no notification for a ringing call while a tab of the app is focused: `onIncoming` has it, and the app (or `palbase/web/calls-ui`) rings.
- **A tap on the notification** focuses a tab of the app, or opens one, and `onIncoming` hears the call ringing as the page opens: the person answers there.
- **When it stops ringing** — missed, or the caller gave up — the missed-call push takes the ringing notification away; a page that is open takes it away as soon as the call no longer rings there (answered on another device too).

How a call rings each platform, the push's data and the missed call are [Ringing](/docs/calls/ringing).

## History

`pb.calls.history(options)` lists this person's calls, the newest first, each with how it went for them (their participant's `state`, `missed` among them): `missed: true` for the ones they missed or were busy for, `state` for those ringing, going on or ended, `limit` (1 to 100, 20 by default) and `cursor` (the previous page's `next_cursor`). `pb.calls.get(callId)` reads one of theirs as it is now.

```ts
// src/missed.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

const { calls, next_cursor } = await pb.calls.history({ missed: true, limit: 50 });
for (const c of calls) console.log(c.created_at, c.video ? "video" : "voice", "from", c.caller_id);
if (next_cursor) console.log("more:", next_cursor);
```

## Permissions and errors

- **The microphone.** Making, answering or joining a call asks for the microphone (and, for video, the camera) first. A refusal rejects with the browser's own error (`NotAllowedError`), and no one is rung, nothing answered. A video call with no camera, or a busy one, goes on by voice.
- **The module's refusals** are a `PalbaseError` (from `palbase/web`), its `code` saying which: `not_allowed` (403: blocks, a conversation's members, your hook), `in_another_call` (409), `too_many_calls` and `quota_exceeded` (429), `invalid_user_ids` and `call_full` (400). Answering a call that is no longer this device's is a `409` too — `answered_elsewhere`, `call_ended`, `not_ringing` — and the session's state shows the call as it is.
- **Not signed in**: `401 not_signed_in`. Calls are the signed-in person's.
- **No WebRTC** (a server, a test without a browser): a `TypeError`. A browser that cannot choose where audio plays (no `setSinkId`) refuses `setAudioOutput` with a `TypeError`.
- **The media later on** — a camera turned on and refused, the media server not reached — is the session's `state.error`, and the call goes on.

## Related

- [Calls](/docs/calls/overview) — kinds of call, who may call whom, a call's life, prices
- [Calls over HTTP](/docs/calls/http) — what the SDK sends
- [Notifications](/docs/web/notifications) — web push and the service worker
- [Error Handling](/docs/web/errors) — `PalbaseError`

# Gateways

Your backend's [gateways](/docs/backend/gateways) are its realtime channels, and an app joins them through the module `palbase apps:sync` writes for it. `pb.<backend>.join(Gateway, params)` resolves once the backend let the user in, with a handle: the gateway's events arrive on it, typed, and its messages go out through it, each answered with the backend's ack. The app writes no channel name, event name or payload type of its own, and a gateway that carries a chat holds the chat's state for the app to render.

## Quick example

```ts
// src/room.ts
import { GatewayError } from "palbase/web";
import { pb, RoomGateway } from "../palbase/shop-web";

// Rejects with a GatewayError (unauthorized) when the backend does not let this user in.
const room = await pb.backend.join(RoomGateway, { roomId: "42" });

room.on("welcome", (w) => console.log(`${w.members} in the room`));
room.on("message", (m) => console.log(`${m.from}: ${m.text}`));

try {
  // Resolves with the ack the backend's @Subscribe returned.
  const { id } = await room.send("say", { text: "hello" });
  console.log("taken as", id);
} catch (e) {
  // The backend's own word (no_commands), or the platform's: forbidden, unavailable, …
  if (e instanceof GatewayError) console.error("not taken:", e.reason);
}

// When the view goes:
room.leave();
```

`RoomGateway` is the backend's class of that name, as the generated module describes it: its pattern `room:{roomId}`, the events it sends and the messages it takes. See the backend's side in [Gateways](/docs/backend/gateways#quick-example).

## The generated module

`palbase apps:sync <app>` writes the checkout's apps their settings and their backends' clients under `palbase/`, from what the project serves now ([The generated module](/docs/web/backend-calls#the-generated-module)). For a web app it writes `palbase/<app>.ts`, which exports the app's `pb`, and a module for each backend the app reaches. With one backend, `palbase/<app>.ts` exports that backend's types and gateways too; with several, each backend's are in `palbase/palbe/<machine>.ts`. Each gateway is a descriptor named by its class. Run the sync again when the backend changes a gateway, and a payload the backend no longer takes is a compile error in the app.

`pb.<backend>` is the machine's name camelCased: `pb.backend` for the machine named `backend`, `pb.shopApi` for `shop-api`. `palbase apps:sync --as shop-api=shop` names it otherwise.

What the app imports from it, cut to the gateways this page uses:

```ts
// palbase/shop-web.ts
// Code generated by palbase apps:sync — DO NOT EDIT. (Cut to this page's gateways.)
import { createClient, type BackendBase, type PalbaseClient } from "palbase/web";
import { __registerBackend } from "palbase/web/palbe";

export interface OrderUpdatesStatusEvent {
  orderId: string;
  status: "paid" | "packed" | "shipped" | "delivered";
}

export type OrderUpdatesEvent =
  | { event: "status"; payload: OrderUpdatesStatusEvent };

export interface OrderUpdatesParams { userId: string }
export const OrderUpdates = {
  name: "OrderUpdates",
  pattern: "orders:{userId}",
  params: ["userId"] as const,
  durable: true,
  events: ["status"] as const,
  messages: [] as const,
  send: {} as {},
  reply: {} as {},
  event: {} as OrderUpdatesEvent,
} as const;

export interface RoomGatewayMessageEvent {
  from: string;
  id: string;
  text: string;
}

export interface RoomGatewayWelcomeEvent {
  members: number;
}

export interface RoomGatewaySayMessage {
  text: string;
}

export interface RoomGatewaySayReply {
  id: string;
}

export type RoomGatewayEvent =
  | { event: "message"; payload: RoomGatewayMessageEvent }
  | { event: "welcome"; payload: RoomGatewayWelcomeEvent };

export interface RoomGatewayParams { roomId: string }
export const RoomGateway = {
  name: "RoomGateway",
  pattern: "room:{roomId}",
  params: ["roomId"] as const,
  durable: false,
  events: ["message", "welcome"] as const,
  messages: ["say"] as const,
  send: {} as { say: RoomGatewaySayMessage },
  reply: {} as { say: RoomGatewaySayReply },
  event: {} as RoomGatewayEvent,
} as const;

export interface SupportGatewayChatEvent {
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
  id?: number;
  type: string;
}

export interface SupportGatewayAnswerMessage {
  callId: string;
  output: string;
}

export interface SupportGatewayDecideMessage {
  approvalId: string;
  approve: boolean;
  reason?: string;
}

export interface SupportGatewaySayMessage {
  clientId?: string;
  delivery?: "next" | "now";
  text: string;
}

export interface SupportGatewaySayReply {
  clientId: string;
}

export type SupportGatewayStopMessage = Record<string, unknown>;

export interface SupportGatewayStopReply {
  stopped: string | null;
}

export type SupportGatewayEvent =
  | { event: "chat"; payload: SupportGatewayChatEvent };

export interface SupportGatewayParams { chatId: string }
export const SupportGateway = {
  name: "SupportGateway",
  pattern: "support:{chatId}",
  params: ["chatId"] as const,
  durable: true,
  chat: true,
  events: ["chat"] as const,
  messages: ["answer", "decide", "say", "stop"] as const,
  send: {} as { answer: SupportGatewayAnswerMessage; decide: SupportGatewayDecideMessage; say: SupportGatewaySayMessage; stop: SupportGatewayStopMessage },
  reply: {} as { answer: unknown; decide: unknown; say: SupportGatewaySayReply; stop: SupportGatewayStopReply },
  event: {} as SupportGatewayEvent,
} as const;

// The backend, for the clients of this environment's project alone. Its routes are in the tree too: see Calling Your Backend.
__registerBackend("https://k3xq81w4m.palbase.studio", "backend", "backend", "https://k3xq81w4m.app.palbase.studio", {});

export interface Backend extends BackendBase {}

export const settings = { url: "https://k3xq81w4m.palbase.studio", publishableKey: "pb_k3xq81w4m_cZ8yX7wV6uT5" } as const;

/** The app's client: the project's modules (pb.auth, …) and its backend, pb.backend. The module makes it on first use (connect). */
export const pb = createClient({ url: settings.url, publishableKey: settings.publishableKey }) as PalbaseClient & { backend: Backend };
```

`send`, `reply` and `event` carry types alone: a `send` is checked against the message's shape and resolves with its ack's, and an event handler is typed by the event. The lists of names are there for a JavaScript caller, which has no compiler: a message or an event the gateway does not declare throws a `TypeError` before anything is sent.

`palbase apps:sync` writes an iOS or Android app in the checkout the same gateways: `pb.backend.join(…)` in Swift and in Kotlin, and in both a chat gateway's handle holds `handle.chat` ([iOS](/docs/ios/gateways), [Android](/docs/android/gateways)).

## Joining

`join(Gateway, params, options?)` takes the gateway's descriptor and a value for each of its pattern's `{param}`s, each one segment of the channel's name: empty, or holding a `:`, it throws a `TypeError`. It opens the project's socket if it is not open, and resolves once the backend let the signed-in user in.

| Member of the handle | What it does |
|---|---|
| `on(event, handler)` | Listens to one event, its payload typed. Returns the function that stops it. |
| `on(handler)` | Listens to every event the gateway declares, as a union to `switch` over. |
| `off(subscription)` | Stops one listener, as calling it does. |
| `send(message, payload)` | Sends one message and waits for the backend to take it: its ack, or a `GatewayError`. |
| `leave()` | Drops the handle's listeners and lets go of the channel. |
| `topic` | The channel: `room:42`. |
| `seq` | A durable gateway's number of the last event the handle was sent. |
| `chat` | A chat gateway's chat. See [Chat gateways](#chat-gateways). |

Hold a handle for as long as its view is on screen, and leave it when the view goes: a gateway with members is one its backend still runs for (what its `@OnFirst` started stops when the last member leaves). Two handles of the same channel share one membership, and the channel is left with the last of them.

Only a signed-in user joins: the access token the socket carries is who they are. The socket is one person's, and it closes when someone signs in or out ([Realtime](/docs/web/realtime#one-socket-one-user)).

## Events

```ts
// src/room-feed.ts
import { pb, RoomGateway, type RoomGatewayEvent } from "../palbase/shop-web";

export async function follow(roomId: string, render: (line: string) => void): Promise<() => void> {
  const room = await pb.backend.join(RoomGateway, { roomId });
  room.on((e: RoomGatewayEvent) => {
    switch (e.event) {
      case "message":
        render(`${e.payload.from}: ${e.payload.text}`);
        break;
      case "welcome":
        render(`${e.payload.members} in the room`);
        break;
    }
  });
  return () => room.leave();
}
```

An event the generated module does not know, from a backend that moved ahead of it, is not delivered. A listener that throws does not take the socket down.

## Messages and acks

`send` resolves with what the backend's `@Subscribe` returned, as its `reply` schema types it, or with nothing when it returned nothing. It rejects with a `GatewayError` whose `reason` says why the message was not taken:

| `reason` | What it means |
|---|---|
| The backend's own word | Its method threw `GatewayRefusal("…")`: `no_commands`, `not_your_turn`, `too_many_messages`. Act on it. |
| `handler_failed` | The method threw something else. The details are in the backend's log. |
| `reply_too_large` | The ack was past 64 KiB. |
| The schema's issues | The payload did not fit the message's schema, said as text (`text: Too small: …`). |
| `forbidden` | The user may only listen on this channel, or the platform refused with no reason given. |
| `rate_limited` | Past the project's events per second. |
| `unavailable` | The backend could not be asked just then. Worth trying again. |
| `no reply`, `socket closed` | No answer came. The message may have been taken. |
| `not joined` | Nothing was sent: the handle was left, its socket closed for good, or the socket is being opened again. |

A join that is refused rejects with a `GatewayError` too: `unauthorized` when the backend did not let the user in (final), `unavailable` when it could not be asked (worth trying again), and `rate_limited` or `too_many_channels` past the project's limits.

A message goes to the backend alone, never to the other members. They hear what the backend emits.

## Durable gateways

A [durable gateway](/docs/backend/gateways#durable-gateways) keeps what it sends. A handle that joins one is sent what it keeps first, in order, then what comes after. `{ history: false }` asks for only what comes after the join:

```ts
// src/orders.ts
import { OrderUpdates, pb } from "../palbase/shop-web";

export async function watchOrders(userId: string, onStatus: (orderId: string, status: string) => void): Promise<() => void> {
  // Only what happens from now: the page reads the orders' current state from the backend's routes.
  const orders = await pb.backend.join(OrderUpdates, { userId }, { history: false });
  orders.on("status", (s) => onStatus(s.orderId, s.status));
  return () => orders.leave();
}
```

The channel's first handle decides: a second handle of the same channel gets the events from where it joins. `handle.seq` is the number of the last event the handle was sent. When the socket drops, the channel is joined again after that number: the handle is sent what it missed, in order, and nothing twice.

## When the connection drops

The socket reconnects by itself ([Realtime](/docs/web/realtime#when-the-connection-drops)), and every gateway that was joined is joined again with it. Meanwhile a `send` answers `not joined`. An event a gateway that is not durable sent while the socket was down is not delivered.

When the socket closes for good (a sign-out, or another user's sign-in) every handle on it ends: its listeners are dropped, and `send` answers `not joined`. Join again, as the user who is there now.

## Chat gateways

A gateway declared with `chat: true` carries a chat of the project's agents, which the platform writes into its channel ([AI](/docs/backend/ai#a-chat-in-an-app)). Its handle has `chat`, the chat's state folded from what the platform writes there: from the chat's start, since the channel keeps it, and then each change as it comes.

| Member of `handle.chat` | What it is |
|---|---|
| `state` | The chat now. The same object until something changes. |
| `subscribe(listener)` | Told each time the state changes, at most once a microtask. Returns the unsubscribe. |
| `for await (const state of handle.chat)` | The state now, then each change, until the gateway is left. |
| `hasOlder`, `loadOlder({ limit? })` | The channel keeps a day of the chat. `loadOlder` reads the page before what the state holds, with the member's own session, and folds it in; it resolves with `hasOlder`, `false` once a page reaches the chat's start. |

What `state` holds:

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `items` | The conversation in order, each one of four types: `{ type: "message", message }`, `{ type: "response", response }`, `{ type: "goal", goal }` (a word of the chat's goal: set, changed, a turn of it begun, judged or checked, its status, cleared) and `{ type: "voice", voice }` (the chat's voice began or ended). A subagent's answer is a part of its parent's. |
| `messages` | Each member's (or the server's) message: `clientId`, `text`, `author` (`null`: the server), `authorName`, `status` (`pending` until the agent has it, then `delivered`, or `failed` with its `error`), `kind` (`text`, or `voice` for a line said in the chat's voice), `attachments` (its pictures and files), `metadata`, `createdAt`, and `mine`. |
| `responses` | Each answer, the subagents' too: `id`, `status` (`running`, `waiting`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, `timed_out`, `budget_exceeded`), `end` and `error` once it ended, `text` so far, `parts`, `thinking` (the model's reasoning step by step, when the agent shows it), `goal` (the goal's turn it is, or `null`), `startedBy`, and `mine`. |
| `turn` | The last turn's state, and what it waits for: `approval`, `tool_output`, `subagents` or `message`. |
| `waiting` | What waits for the signed-in user: `approvals`, the tool calls of their own turns waiting for their yes, and `outputs`, their own turns' client tool calls waiting for their app's answer. Another member's turn is theirs. |
| `goal` | The chat's goal once one was set: `objective`, `status` (`active`, `paused`, `blocked`, `budget_limited`, `achieved`, or `cleared`), its stop code and reason, and its `events`. `null` without one. |
| `voice` | The chat's voice, the last that began in it, live or ended: `status` (`started`, `closed`), `mine`, `seconds` and `closeReason` once it closed. `null` without one. |
| `forkedFrom` | A fork's: `{ chatId, beforeMessage }`, the chat it was forked from. `null` for a chat of its own. |

An answer's `parts` are its pieces in order, each one of four types: `{ type: "text", text }`; `{ type: "tool", tool }`, a tool call; `{ type: "agent", agent }`, a subagent handed work (or refused it, `status: "denied"` with its `reason`); and `{ type: "thinking", thinking }`, a step's reasoning (`text`, or `unavailable: true` with the provider's `reason` when the agent shows its reasoning and the provider gave none). A render that leaves a type out leaves that piece of the conversation out.

`mine` is the signed-in user's: a message they wrote, an answer to a turn they began. A tool call (a `tool` part, or one of `waiting`) has `call_id`, `name`, `status`, `input`, `output` and, while it waits for a yes, `approval_id`. Its `output` is the answer's last 16 KiB: `omittedBytes` says how much came before it, and `pb.chatToolCall(chatId, callId)` reads the whole answer.

What the member does in the chat goes through the gateway's own messages, and the backend does it as them: `say`, `decide` (an approval's yes or no), `answer` (a client tool's output) and `stop`, in the backend of [AI](/docs/backend/ai#a-chat-in-an-app). A refusal is its reason: `not_your_turn`, `too_many_messages`, `history_full`.

A chat in React:

```tsx
// src/support/SupportChat.tsx
import { useEffect, useState, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import { GatewayError, type ChatItem, type ChatPart, type ChatResponse, type ChatState, type GatewayChat } from "palbase/web";
import { pb, SupportGateway } from "../../palbase/shop-web";

const joinSupport = (chatId: string) => pb.backend.join(SupportGateway, { chatId });
type Support = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof joinSupport>>;

function useChat(chat: GatewayChat): ChatState {
  return useSyncExternalStore((changed) => chat.subscribe(changed), () => chat.state);
}

export function SupportChat({ chatId }: { chatId: string }) {
  const [support, setSupport] = useState<Support | null>(null);
  const [refused, setRefused] = useState<string | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    let gone = false;
    let held: Support | undefined;
    joinSupport(chatId).then(
      (h) => (gone ? h.leave() : setSupport((held = h))),
      (e: unknown) => setRefused(e instanceof GatewayError ? e.reason : "unavailable"),
    );
    return () => {
      gone = true;
      held?.leave();
    };
  }, [chatId]);
  if (refused) return <p>The chat did not open: {refused}</p>;
  return support ? <Conversation support={support} /> : <p>Opening…</p>;
}

function Conversation({ support }: { support: Support }) {
  const state = useChat(support.chat);
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState("");
  const [problem, setProblem] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const act = (work: Promise<unknown>) => work.catch((e: unknown) => setProblem(e instanceof GatewayError ? e.reason : "unavailable"));
  return (
    <section>
      {support.chat.hasOlder && <button onClick={() => void support.chat.loadOlder()}>Earlier messages</button>}
      {state.goal && <p className="goal">Goal: {state.goal.objective} ({state.goal.status})</p>}
      {state.items.map((item, i) => <Item key={keyOf(item, i)} item={item} />)}
      {state.waiting.approvals.map((call) => {
        const approvalId = call.approval_id;
        return approvalId ? (
          <p key={call.call_id}>
            The assistant asks to run {call.name}.
            <button onClick={() => act(support.send("decide", { approvalId, approve: true }))}>Allow</button>
            <button onClick={() => act(support.send("decide", { approvalId, approve: false, reason: "Not now." }))}>Deny</button>
          </p>
        ) : null;
      })}
      {problem && <p role="alert">{problem}</p>}
      <form
        onSubmit={(e) => {
          e.preventDefault();
          setProblem(null);
          void act(support.send("say", { text: draft }).then(() => setDraft("")));
        }}
      >
        <input value={draft} onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)} />
        <button type="submit">Send</button>
        <button type="button" onClick={() => act(support.send("stop", {}))}>Stop</button>
      </form>
    </section>
  );
}

function keyOf(item: ChatItem, i: number): string {
  switch (item.type) {
    case "message":
      return `m:${item.message.clientId}`;
    case "response":
      return `r:${item.response.id}`;
    case "goal":
      return `g:${item.goal.seq}:${i}`;
    case "voice":
      return `v:${item.voice.voice_id}:${item.voice.status}`;
  }
}

function Item({ item }: { item: ChatItem }) {
  switch (item.type) {
    case "message": {
      const m = item.message;
      return (
        <p className={m.mine ? "mine" : "theirs"}>
          <b>{m.authorName || "Support"}</b> {m.kind === "voice" ? "(said) " : ""}
          {m.text}
          {m.attachments.map((a) => <small key={a.position}> [{a.name}]</small>)}
          {m.status === "pending" ? " …" : m.status === "failed" ? ` (not delivered: ${m.error ?? "failed"})` : ""}
        </p>
      );
    }
    case "response":
      return <Answer response={item.response} />;
    case "goal":
      return <small className="goal">Goal: {item.goal.kind}{item.goal.goal ? `, ${item.goal.goal.status}` : ""}</small>;
    case "voice":
      return <small>{item.voice.status === "started" ? "A voice call began" : `The voice call ended after ${item.voice.seconds ?? 0} s`}</small>;
  }
}

function Part({ part }: { part: ChatPart }) {
  switch (part.type) {
    case "text":
      return <p>{part.text}</p>;
    case "thinking":
      return part.thinking.unavailable ? (
        <small>No reasoning shown: {part.thinking.reason ?? "the provider gave none"}</small>
      ) : (
        <details>
          <summary>Thinking</summary>
          {part.thinking.text}
        </details>
      );
    case "tool":
      return <small>{part.tool.name}: {part.tool.status}</small>;
    case "agent":
      return <small>{part.agent.name}: {part.agent.status === "denied" ? `refused (${part.agent.reason ?? ""})` : "working"}</small>;
  }
}

function Answer({ response }: { response: ChatResponse }) {
  return (
    <div className="answer">
      {response.parts.map((part, i) => <Part key={i} part={part} />)}
      {response.end === "budget_exceeded" && <small>This answer reached its budget.</small>}
      {response.end === "failed" && <small>This answer failed.</small>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

A client tool's call waits in `state.waiting.outputs` until the app answers it, once:

```ts
// src/support/pick-city.ts
import type { ChatState } from "palbase/web";
import { pb, SupportGateway } from "../../palbase/shop-web";

export async function answerCities(chatId: string, pick: (reason: string) => Promise<string>): Promise<() => void> {
  const support = await pb.backend.join(SupportGateway, { chatId });
  const answering = new Set<string>();
  const stop = support.chat.subscribe((state: ChatState) => {
    for (const call of state.waiting.outputs) {
      if (call.name !== "pick_city" || answering.has(call.call_id)) continue;
      answering.add(call.call_id);
      const { reason } = call.input as { reason: string };
      void pick(reason).then((city) => support.send("answer", { callId: call.call_id, output: city }));
    }
  });
  return () => {
    stop();
    support.leave();
  };
}
```

# Analytics

`pb.analytics` sends the project's analytics module what the app's people do: the events it captures, page views, and what it knows of the person. It holds events and sends them together, a few seconds apart or twenty at a time, and a page that closes sends what it holds as it goes. With the `analytics` option of `createClient` it also records the browser's own measures: a page view per address, web vitals and the page's request timings. Nothing is collected that the person has not allowed: events, page views and person properties go only with the `analytics` key granted, the browser's timings only with `performance` ([Consent](/docs/web/consent)). What the project reads back (summaries, event lists, funnels, retention, people) is the secret key's, and Studio's Analytics screens show it.

## Quick example

```ts
// src/lib/palbase.ts
import { createClient } from "palbase/web";

export const pb = createClient({
  url: "https://k3xq81w4m.palbase.studio",
  publishableKey: "pb_k3xq81w4m_cZ8yX7wV6uT5",
  // Page views, web vitals and request timings, recorded by the client; the app's version kept with every event.
  analytics: { appVersion: "2.4.1" },
  // Collected before the person chooses. Where the law asks first, start them denied and ask: see Consent.
  consent: { start: { analytics: "granted", performance: "granted" } },
});
```

```ts
// src/checkout.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

pb.analytics.capture("checkout_started", { plan: "pro", items: 3 });

// What is known of the person: the signed-in user, or this browser's anonymous visitor.
await pb.analytics.people.set({ plan: "pro" });
await pb.analytics.people.setOnce({ first_plan: "pro" });
await pb.analytics.people.add({ checkouts: 1 });

// A view the address does not show (a dialog, a step of a wizard).
pb.analytics.page({ title: "Checkout: payment" });
```

The calls go from the browser straight to the project's address, which answers a page on any site. See [Overview](/docs/web/overview#calling-the-project-from-a-browser).

## `pb.analytics`

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `capture(event, properties?)` | Records an event: a name (a letter or `$`, then letters, digits and `_.:-$`, 64 at most) and its properties. |
| `page({ url?, title?, referrer?, properties? })` | Records a `$pageview`: the page's address unless given, its title, where the visitor came from. |
| `people.set`, `people.setOnce`, `people.unset`, `people.add` | Sets the person's properties, sets the ones not set already, removes some, adds to numbers. |
| `identify(traits?)` | Ties this browser's anonymous events to the signed-in user, with their traits. The client does it on its own when someone signs in. |
| `reset()` | Forgets this browser's anonymous id and session: the next visitor is someone new. The client does it on its own when someone signs out. |
| `flush()` | Sends what is held now. |
| `start(options?)` | Starts the browser's own measures, as the `analytics` option does: `pageViews`, `webVitals`, `network`, each on unless turned off. Returns what stops them. |
| `onEvent(listener)` | Told of each event the app captures, here in the page, whatever the person chose: what in-app messages are triggered by. Nothing leaves the page for it. |

An event is the signed-in user's when someone is signed in, and this browser's anonymous visitor's otherwise; once they sign in, their anonymous history is theirs. A session is half an hour without an event.

What the client reads on its own goes as the page's **route**, not its address: no query, no fragment, and a path segment that is not a word of the route (a number, an id, an email, a token) becomes `:id`. `/orders/8f1c…/receipt?token=…` is sent as `/orders/:id/receipt`. The browser's referrer is cut the same way, since on a same-site arrival it is the whole previous address. What your code passes to `page()` is sent as you passed it.

The browser's own measures, once started:

| Measure | What it is | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Page views | A `$pageview` for the first page and each navigation after it (history and back/forward). | `analytics` |
| Web vitals | LCP, CLS, INP, FCP and TTFB, as `web_vital` samples. | `performance` |
| Request timings | Each `fetch` the page makes: method, address without its query, status, time. | `performance` |

A timing goes without the person's id unless `analytics` is granted too. Refusing a key drops what was held of it at once.

## What an app sends

The client makes these calls for you. They are the analytics module's, with the publishable key over HTTPS, and a signed-in user's token makes what they send theirs:

| Call | What it is | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /analytics/capture` | One event | `{ event, distinct_id, properties?, session_id?, app_version?, timestamp?, sent_at? }` |
| `POST /analytics/batch` | Up to 100 events, 3 MiB | `{ events: [<capture bodies>] }` |
| `POST /analytics/page` | A `$pageview` | `{ distinct_id, url, title?, referrer?, properties?, session_id?, … }` |
| `POST /analytics/screen` | A `$screen` | `{ distinct_id, screen_name, properties?, session_id?, … }` |
| `POST /analytics/identify` | An `$identify`: who the user is | `{ distinct_id, anonymous_id?, traits? }` |
| `POST /analytics/alias` | An `$alias`: two ids are one user | `{ from, to }` |
| `POST /analytics/people` | The person's properties | `{ set?, set_once?, unset?, add? }` |
| `POST /analytics/perf` | Up to 100 samples, 512 KiB: web vitals, request timings | `{ items: [ … ] }` |

- **`event`**: a letter or `$`, then letters, digits and `_.:-$`, 64 characters at most.
- **`distinct_id`**: who did it, 256 characters at most, with no NUL character. With a user's token the user's id is the distinct id, whatever the body says, so a signed-in user's events are theirs however the app wrote them.
- **`properties`** and **`traits`**: 100 at most, 8 KiB each as JSON, 32 KiB in all.
- **`timestamp`** and **`sent_at`**: unix milliseconds on the device's clock. The difference between `sent_at` and the server's clock is the device clock's error, and it is taken off `timestamp`. An event queued offline keeps its own `timestamp` and gets a fresh `sent_at` when it goes out.
- **`identify`'s `anonymous_id`**: the id the user had before signing in. Their anonymous history goes with them, and if they are deleted, it goes too.
- **`user_id`** (capture and batch): your server, with its secret key, says whose an event is — something a user did that your backend saw (a document approved, an order shipped). The event is that user's, as if their app had sent it signed in: on their timeline (source `server`), in their funnels, and acted on by their [journeys](/docs/backend/journeys#from-your-backend). `distinct_id` may be left out then. An app's event is its signed-in user's: one that names `user_id` is refused (`400 invalid_user_id`).

The headers say what the server cannot tell from the body:

| Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `idempotency-key` | The same key sent again within two minutes is not kept twice. Send one per event, and send it again with a retry. |
| `x-platform` | `web`, `ios` or `android`, kept with the event. |
| `x-palbase-client-version` | Your app's version, kept with the event. |
| `x-os-version` | The operating system's version. |
| `x-palbase-installation` | The install it came from (`pb.installation.id`): the platform's events about the install — a push that reached it while no one was signed in — are its person's. Sent only with `analytics` granted. |

## What comes back

A call is answered once what it sent is kept: on the platform's stream, written to the store within seconds, even while the store restarts. So a `202` means the event will be there.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `202` | Kept. A batch answers it when every event was kept. |
| `207` | A batch with some events refused: `{ accepted, rejected: [{ index, error, error_description }] }`. The rest were kept. |
| `400` | The body does not fit the rules above. A batch none of whose events was kept answers its first refusal. |
| `413` | Over the size limits. |
| `429` | Over what the project may send per second, all kinds together. `Retry-After` says when. |
| `503` | Not kept: send again with the same `idempotency-key`. |

What an app sends is counted against its own budget, per project per second, not against the requests the rest of the project's calls may make.

## Consent

Analytics follows what the person allowed, kept by `pb.consent`: events, page views, `identify` and person properties go only with `analytics` granted; web vitals and request timings with `performance`, and without the person's id unless `analytics` is granted too. A key with neither the person's choice nor a starting value collects nothing. Every call that carries the person's data says the install it came from, `X-Palbase-Installation`. See [Consent](/docs/web/consent) for the keys, the starting values and a consent screen.

A user's analytics go when the user is deleted — everything under any id they went by, and the install's events from while no one was signed in. The project's analytics settings (`PUT /analytics/settings`, with the secret key) say how long events are kept: 90 days unless changed.

## People

The anonymous id an app had before its person signed up is that person once `identify` names it: their events before and after are one person's in funnels, retention and their timeline. Properties are set of a person with `POST /analytics/people` (`{ set?, set_once?, unset?, add? }`; the client's `pb.analytics.people.set`, `setOnce`, `unset` and `add`): a signed-in user's are theirs, an anonymous visitor's are their anonymous id's. Where an install came from (`$initial_utm_source`, `$initial_referrer` …) is set once of the person who installed.

The project's server reads them with the secret key: `GET /analytics/people?query=…` finds a person by any id they went by or their email, `GET /analytics/people/{person_id}` is their profile — with where they were last ([Where a person is](#where-a-person-is)) — and `GET /analytics/people/{person_id}/events` their timeline, newest first — what their apps sent, what their backend sent, and what Palbase did for them (a purchase, a push that reached their phone, a consent changed). `GET /analytics/catalog` lists every event a timeline can hold: Palbase's, with their fields, and the app's own as they arrived; `PUT /analytics/catalog/{name}` describes or hides one. Studio's **People** and **Event catalog** screens show the same.

## Where a person is

Each event is given the place of the address it came from — the user's own, because the browser sends it to the project directly: its `country` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), its `region` (a province or state, by its English name) and its `city` (a city or district). A person's profile says where their newest event that had a place came from; a summary breaks down by each of the three; an audience can pick people by them. Places come from DB-IP's IP to City Lite database: IP geolocation by [DB-IP](https://db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0. An address says where its network is, not the device: a phone on mobile data is often placed in its carrier's city.

## Audiences

An audience is the people a rule picks, among those behind the project's events. Its members are worked out when it is made or changed, then every minute, and each person who enters or leaves it from then on is told: `audience.entered` and `audience.exited` (`{ audience_id, audience_name, person_id, user_id }`) go into their timeline, to your webhook and to your backend's `@On` handlers. Its first members are not told they entered — the rule came to them, they did nothing — and neither is anyone when it is deleted. A push can go to an audience's members ([Notifications](/docs/backend/notifications#to-an-audience)).

The secret key's calls:

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /analytics/audiences` | Makes one: `{ name, description?, rule }`. A project keeps 100 at most. |
| `POST /analytics/audiences/preview` | Who a rule would pick now, without keeping it: how many, and the first twenty. A rule that takes longer than 20 seconds to work out answers `422 preview_too_slow`. |
| `GET /analytics/audiences`, `GET /analytics/audiences/{id}` | Each audience with its rule, how many are in it, when it was last worked out, and `state`: `ready`, or `pending` while a rule made or changed is worked out. |
| `PATCH /analytics/audiences/{id}` | Changes its name, description or rule. A changed rule is worked out anew, and, like a new one, tells no one at once. |
| `GET /analytics/audiences/{id}/members` | A page of its members: each one's person id, the user they signed in as, and the installs their events came from. |
| `DELETE /analytics/audiences/{id}` | Deletes it and its members. |

A rule is one to twenty conditions, every one of which holds (`match: "all"`, unless said) or at least one (`"any"`):

```json
{
  "match": "all",
  "conditions": [
    { "type": "event", "event": "purchase", "did": false, "within": { "amount": 7, "unit": "days" } },
    { "type": "event", "event": "app_opened", "did": true, "at_least": 3, "within": { "amount": 30, "unit": "days" } },
    { "type": "property", "key": "plan", "op": "neq", "value": "pro" },
    { "type": "place", "field": "city", "op": "in", "value": ["Istanbul", "Kadıköy"] },
    { "type": "platform", "op": "eq", "value": "ios" }
  ]
}
```

| Condition | Picks a person who… |
|---|---|
| `event` | did (`did: true`, `at_least` times, 1 unless said) or did not (`did: false`) an event in the last `within`: `amount` `minutes`, `hours` or `days`, a year at most. The event is an app's own or one of Palbase's (`purchases.purchase.completed`, `notification.opened` …). |
| `property` | has a property: `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte` (numbers), `contains` (text, any case), `set`, `not_set`. |
| `place` | was last in a `country`, `region` or `city`: `eq`, `neq`, or `in` a list of up to 50. |
| `platform` | last sent from `ios`, `android` or `web`: `eq`, `neq` or `in`. |

`neq` holds for a person the value is not known of, as not `eq`. A user who is deleted leaves every audience and never comes back to one. Studio's **Analytics › Audiences** screen builds a rule a condition at a time, previews it, and lists each audience's people.

## From the CLI

The secret key's reads and the analytics settings are also commands of the CLI, for the environment it is pointed at (`-E <env>`):

```sh
palbase analytics:summary --window 7d
palbase analytics:events --name checkout_started --window 24h --limit 20
palbase analytics:settings:set retention_days=30
```

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`palbase analytics:summary`](/docs/cli/reference#palbase-analyticssummary) | What analytics counted over a window (`30m`, `24h`, `7d`): events, users, sessions, the top events. |
| [`palbase analytics:events`](/docs/cli/reference#palbase-analyticsevents) | The events recorded, newest first: by name, by user (their distinct id), over a window. |
| [`palbase analytics:settings:get`](/docs/cli/reference#palbase-analyticssettingsget), [`palbase analytics:settings:set`](/docs/cli/reference#palbase-analyticssettingsset) | How long events are kept (`retention_days`), the share of performance samples kept (`perf_sample_pct`), whether bodies are kept (`console_bodies`). A shorter retention removes what is older within minutes. |

# Consent

`pb.consent` keeps what the person allowed the app to collect and use, key by key. A choice stands in the browser the moment it is made — a key refused stops its data at once, before anything else is sent — and goes to the project with when it was made, later if the browser is offline. The project keeps every choice with when and where it was made, and what the SDKs collect follows the keys: [analytics](/docs/web/analytics) sends events only with `analytics` granted, a flag's audience condition and an in-app campaign to an audience reach only who allowed `personalization`, and the project's marketing messages skip whoever refused a channel's marketing key.

## Quick example

```ts
// src/lib/palbase.ts
import { createClient } from "palbase/web";

export const pb = createClient({
  url: "https://k3xq81w4m.palbase.studio",
  publishableKey: "pb_k3xq81w4m_cZ8yX7wV6uT5",
  analytics: true,
  consent: {
    // What is collected before the person chooses: nothing, until they say.
    start: { analytics: "denied", performance: "denied" },
    // The version of the consent text this app shows.
    textVersion: "2026-10",
    // The app's own keys, listed after the platform's.
    customKeys: ["custom.chat_transcripts"],
  },
});
```

```ts
// src/consent-banner.ts
import type { ConsentState } from "palbase/web";
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";

/** Draws a choice for every key the person is still to be asked about. */
export async function showConsentBanner(root: HTMLElement): Promise<void> {
  const ask = new Set(await pb.consent.needsAsking());
  if (ask.size === 0) return;
  const keys = (await pb.consent.keys()).filter((k) => ask.has(k.key));
  const lang = navigator.language.startsWith("tr") ? "tr" : "en";
  const choices: Record<string, ConsentState> = {};
  for (const k of keys) {
    const box = document.createElement("input");
    box.type = "checkbox";
    box.addEventListener("change", () => { choices[k.key] = box.checked ? "granted" : "denied"; });
    choices[k.key] = "denied";
    const label = document.createElement("label");
    // The platform's keys come with their words; the app words its own.
    label.append(box, ` ${k.title[lang] ?? k.key}`);
    root.append(label);
  }
  const save = document.createElement("button");
  save.textContent = "Save";
  // One screen's choices, made together.
  save.addEventListener("click", () => { pb.consent.setMany(choices); root.replaceChildren(); });
  root.append(save);
}
```

```ts
// src/main.ts
import { pb } from "./lib/palbase";
import { showConsentBanner } from "./consent-banner";

await showConsentBanner(document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#consent")!);

// Told of every change: here, in another tab, on another of the person's devices, or by the project.
pb.consent.onChange((key, state) => console.log(key, state ?? "not chosen"));
```

## The keys

The keys a consent screen lists come from the project, the same list for every SDK:

| Key | Category | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| `analytics` | measurement | Events, page views, `identify` and person properties. |
| `performance` | measurement | Web vitals and request timings. |
| `diagnostics` | measurement | What went wrong when the app failed: errors and crashes. |
| `personalization` | personalization | Tailoring what the app shows by what the person does: a flag's audience condition, an in-app campaign to an audience. |
| `marketing_push`, `marketing_email`, `marketing_sms`, `marketing_whatsapp` | marketing | Messages that are not transactional, on that channel. |
| `ads_measurement`, `ads_personalization` | advertising | What US laws call selling or sharing (`ads: true`). |

`keys()` answers them in the order a screen shows them, each `{ key, category, title, description, ads }` with its words in English and Turkish (`title.en`, `title.tr`), then the app's own `customKeys` (`custom.<name>`: a–z, 0–9 and `_`, 48 at most), whose words are the app's (`category: "custom"`). The platform's list is read from the project once (`GET /auth/consents/keys`).

## `pb.consent`

| Member | What it does |
|---|---|
| `keys()` | The platform's keys with their words, then the app's own. |
| `state(key)` | `"granted"`, `"denied"`, or `undefined` when the person has not chosen and the app gave no starting value. While the person's choices are still to be read from the project, it answers `"denied"`. |
| `set(key, state)`, `setMany({ … })` | Records the person's choice, or a screen's choices together. It stands at once and goes to the project with when it was made. |
| `onChange(listener)` | Calls `listener(key, state)` for each key whose state changed: here, in another tab, on another of the person's devices, or by the project on their word. Returns the unsubscribe. |
| `region()` | `{ country?, jurisdiction }`, where `jurisdiction` is `gdpr` (the EU, the EEA, the UK, Switzerland: asked before anything is collected), `us` (collected until refused) or `other`, from the person's address. |
| `lastDeniedAt(key)` | When the key was last refused: here, on another of the person's devices, or by the project. |
| `needsAsking(keys?)` | The keys to ask about: never chosen, or chosen on the app's screen under another `textVersion`. In the US, an advertising key refused within the last twelve months is not asked again. |

## Starting values

`createClient({ consent: { start } })` says what is collected before the person chooses, key by key. The starting values are the app's, and they never leave the browser: only the person's own choices are sent, so a starting value can never undo a refusal the project holds. A key the SDK collects for with neither a choice nor a starting value collects nothing: give `analytics` and `performance` when the app uses them.

Where the law asks first — `region()` answers `gdpr` — start those keys `denied` and ask. An app whose people are all where data is collected until refused may start them `granted`, and still offers the choice. A choice made under one `textVersion` is asked again once the app shows a new text with a new version.

## Whose the choices are

The device's while no one is signed in. On sign-in the device's newer choices become the account's and the device takes the account's: the newest explicit choice wins, never a starting value. On sign-out the device goes back to the app's starting values, and the next person here is asked anew. A refusal made elsewhere — an unsubscribe link, another of the person's devices, the project on their word — reaches the signed-in person's open pages at once, and their keys change here.

A browser that sends Global Privacy Control refuses the advertising keys for the person once, recorded as `gpc`. A choice the person makes in the app after it is theirs.

## The calls under it

`pb.consent` makes these calls for you; an app that makes them itself sends what the client does:

| Call | What it is |
|---|---|
| `GET /auth/consents/keys` | The platform's keys with their words. |
| `GET /auth/consents?installation_id=…` | The choices and the region: the account's with a user's token, the device's with the publishable key alone. |
| `PUT /auth/consents` | `{ installation_id, text_version?, choices: [{ key, state, chosen_at }] }`: records choices, the account's or the device's as above. |
| `POST /auth/consents/link` | On sign-in: the device's newer choices become the account's. |

The last three name the install and prove they hold it with `X-Palbase-Installation-Secret`: the secret the client keeps in the browser, from which the install's id is made (`pb.installation.id`). The device's own choices, asked for or written without the secret it first named itself with, are refused `403 not_the_device`.

The project's server can only refuse, never grant: `POST /admin/consents/refuse` with the secret key (`{ user_id | installation_id, keys, reason }`, reason `email_unsubscribe`, `sms_stop` or `support`) records a refusal the person made elsewhere, and it reaches their apps at once. `GET /admin/users/{uid}/consents` and `GET /admin/installations/{installation_id}/consents` read the state and the proof of each choice. A deleted user's choices go with them.

## Related

- [Analytics](/docs/web/analytics) — what the `analytics` and `performance` keys hold back
- [Flags](/docs/web/flags) — audience conditions, which need `personalization`
- [Notifications](/docs/web/notifications) — in-app campaigns and the marketing keys
- [Notifications in your backend](/docs/backend/notifications) — sends the marketing keys skip
